sections.h2: What is Burke County, Georgia, and who sells homes there?
sections.html:
Burke is among Georgia's original counties, formed on February 5, 1777, and it lies along the state's eastern edge, across from South Carolina. Waynesboro is the seat. Covering 827 square miles of land, it ranks as Georgia's second-biggest county by area and falls inside the Augusta metropolitan area (Wikipedia).

The county's website names seven municipalities: Blythe, Girard, Keysville, Midville, Sardis, Vidette and Waynesboro. It bills Burke as the Bird Dog Capital of the World, with hunting and fishing as a draw.

Mid-2025 population stood at 24,408 per Census QuickFacts, slightly under the 2020 base. The same table shows a median home value of $151,600, owner occupancy of 70 percent and 100 building permits in 2025. Sellers often hold farmland, timber or an older house in town, and in a county this large the parcel can sit a long way from the courthouse.

Schooling comes from the Burke County School District, which Wikipedia lists with a single high school and a single middle school, several lower-grade schools and an alternative school. Wikipedia also gives 11,138 housing units for 2020, of which 11.1 percent were empty.

sections.h2: Where do I go for Burke County property tax business?
sections.html:
Both offices are at 524 Myrick Street in Waynesboro, the Board of Assessors in Suite B and the tax commissioner in Suite A. Assessors set values and, per their page, send no bills and collect nothing. The commissioner collects for the county, the state and the Board of Education, and the commissioner's site says that office has no say in values.

sections.h2: How can a Burke County owner contest a value?
sections.html:
An owner has 45 days from the notice date to appeal, and the commissioner's site describes four routes. The assessor's page says assessment notices are sent to taxpayers in July, so watch the mail then.

  • Board of Equalization. The Board of Assessors sees the appeal first and may revise the value with a new notice. If it does, the owner gets 30 more days to challenge that notice; an appeal left unchanged is passed to the Board of Equalization for a hearing.
  • Hearing officer. Offered only for non-homestead real property above $500,000, with a state-certified appraiser serving as the officer.
  • Arbitration. Say so in your filing, then hand in a certified appraisal within 45 days of the board's acknowledgement, which it must do within 10 days. A hearing is held within 30 days of authorization.
  • Superior Court. Mail or file a written notice with the Board of Assessors inside 30 days of the earlier ruling.

The arbitrator's fees depend on the result. The page states that the county pays if your value is closest to the arbitrator's figure, and you pay if the board's value is closer.

sections.h2: What homestead exemptions does Burke County offer?
sections.html:
Applications are accepted all year at either the commissioner's office or the Board of Assessors, though to count for the current year one must be postmarked or received by the final day of the appeal period. On January 1 you must hold title, live there and claim it as your residence. The commissioner's FAQ names April 1 as the cutoff for the billing year.

The exemptions listed on the county's homestead page include:

  • S1, the standard exemption: $2,000 off assessed value for state, county and school, with no age or income test.
  • S3 and S4, for owners 62 and 65 whose income is under $10,000, which add a $10,000 school exemption.
  • S5, SD, SS and SE, which cover disabled veterans and the unremarried spouses of service members who died in war.
  • SG, for the spouse of a peace officer or firefighter who died on duty.
  • L3 and L4 local school exemptions for owners 65 and older.

A refinance leaves an exemption alone unless the name on the deed changes. Vehicles you own must also be registered in Burke County. The Burke County Board of Commissioners, the Board of Education and the cities of Waynesboro, Sardis, Girard, Midville and Keysville have opted out of the statewide floating exemption.

sections.h2: How does payment work in Burke County?
sections.html:
Accepted forms of payment include cash, checks, money orders and major cards, with a convenience fee on cards. You may also pay on the website or by calling 1-844-898-2374 with your bill number.

Several FAQ answers matter to anyone selling:

  • A part payment is accepted, yet interest and penalty continue on whatever is left.
  • When a parcel faces a tax lien sale, phone the commissioner before sending a part payment.
  • Appealing does not stop billing. Accounts under appeal are billed at 85 percent of the property's market value and corrected after the final ruling.
  • A surviving spouse may petition for a year's support through an attorney or the probate court.

A non-homestead mobile home in the county on January 1 owes tax and must show a current decal. Unpaid taxes draw a 10 percent penalty plus interest, and a missing decal carries a fine of $100 to $300.

sections.h2: What becomes of unpaid Burke County taxes?
sections.html:
Delinquent parcels can be sold at tax sale. The commissioner's site posted October 6, 2026 as a sale date with a parcel list, so the date has passed. The commissioner's home page links to that sale's parcel list.

Before listing, look up the parcel number on the commissioner's site and make sure no earlier year is open. Returns are taken January 1 through April 1, and tangible personal property worth $7,500 or less in fair market value is exempt, though motor vehicles, trailers and mobile homes are not. A buyer's attorney will check the real property bill and any personal property or mobile home account tied to the address.

For the figure due at closing, request a written payoff from the commissioner, and have the closing agent explain how this year's bill is shared.

faqs.q: Where does a Burke County resident pay in person?
faqs.a: At the tax commissioner, 524 Myrick Street, Suite A, Waynesboro. The number is 706-554-3223. Weekdays run 8:30 to 5, and two Saturdays a month, the first and third, the office opens 9 to noon.

faqs.q: How soon must a Burke County appeal be filed?
faqs.a: File within 45 days of the notice date. Should the Board of Assessors amend the value, a further 30 days applies to the amended notice.

faqs.q: Must I pay my Burke County tax bill during an appeal?
faqs.a: Yes. Accounts under appeal are billed at 85 percent of the property's market value, and the county corrects the bill after the final decision.

faqs.q: Is a part payment accepted in Burke County?
faqs.a: Yes, though interest and penalty keep running on the remainder. If the parcel faces a tax lien sale, call the commissioner first.

faqs.q: What does the Burke County standard homestead exemption cover?
faqs.a: The S1 exemption removes $2,000 from assessed value for state, county and school taxes, with no age or income test. The owner must be in residence on January 1 and apply by April 1.
